relationships.name: Lowest cost bidding (Meta / Paid Social)
relationships.difference: Lowest cost bidding gets the most results for the budget without limiting bid amount; Target ROAS instead bids to reach an average return on ad spend the advertiser chooses, so it needs conversion values rather than just event counts.
relationships.context: Shopping on Google Ads, where the advertiser optimizes toward a return-on-ad-spend target.

evidence.locator: Field bid_strategy: 'LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP: Designed to get the most results for your budget based on your ad set optimization_goal without limiting your bid amount... also known as automatic bidding'

relationships.name: Cost cap bidding (Meta / Paid Social)
relationships.difference: Meta's cost cap limits the actual average cost per optimization event to a specified amount; Target ROAS optimizes conversion value against an average return on ad spend, which is a value-efficiency goal, not a cost-per-event cap.
relationships.context: Shopping on Google Ads with a revenue-efficiency objective rather than a per-event cost objective.

evidence.locator: Field bid_strategy: 'COST_CAP: Designed to get the most results for your budget based on your ad set optimization_goal while limiting actual average cost per optimization event'
